subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Brooks <aiden.brooks@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)

Hi Aiden —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Pain points / constraints you mentioned:
- Strong PII handling requirements: customer identifiers, financial account numbers, and support transcripts must be classified and not retained longer than policy allows.
- Need audit-grade request/response logging with immutable timestamps and ability to export logs to your SIEM (Splunk).
- Redaction requirements: redact sensitive fields before logs leave a network boundary or be able to configure automatic redaction on ingest.
- Retention policy: default retention 90 days, ability to purge specific records on request.

Current stack & notes from your side:
- Ingest pipeline -> Kinesis -> S3 (encrypted) -> Splunk for centralized logs.
- Internal models used for enrichment; exploring third-party inference for customer-facing features.
- SOC2 Type II and internal security review coming up in Q1.

Success criteria for a proof-of-concept (PoC):
1) Demonstrate that inference requests can be routed through your VPC with private networking (VPC peering or PrivateLink).
2) Show request/response logging that can be delivered to your S3 bucket and consumed by Splunk; logs must include immutable timestamps and request IDs.
3) Provide configurable PII redaction or a pre-send redactor hook so PII never persists to long-term logs.
4) Document retention and purge workflow that satisfies your legal/compliance team (90-day default + on-demand purge).

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- I’ll share our SOC2 summary and a short logging playbook (see attachments).
- Neha will schedule a technical deep-dive next week with your infra/security engineers to discuss VPC/networking options and KMS integration.
- Vivek to prepare a draft mutual action plan and an initial architecture diagram showing logging export paths.

Attachments: SOC2_report_v3.pdf (summary), logging_playbook.pdf (how our logs/export work + redaction options).

Would love confirmation that the above aligns with your notes and any gaps you want us to include before the technical call.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference

From: Aiden Brooks <aiden.brooks@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Security <security@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)

Marissa —

This is a good summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our side:
- Retention: 90 days is correct for general logs, but audit logs tied to billing events need to be kept for 1 year. We’ll want to ensure we can tag logs appropriately so retention rules differ by tag.
- Redaction: Ideally we’d like an SDK-level redactor plus the ability to set server-side redaction rules. Can you confirm both are available in the PoC?
- Encryption/KMS: We use AWS KMS; customer-managed keys (CMKs) are preferred. Is that supported for S3 exports and any long-term storage of logs?

Security (cc’d) — our security engineer, Jen (security@acmecorp.com), will pick a couple of times for the technical call.

If you can confirm the redaction and KMS details, we’ll accept the PoC scope and provide times for next week.

Thanks,
Aiden Brooks
Head of Product, Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aiden Brooks <aiden.brooks@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: data privacy & logging requirements (Acme Corp)

Thanks Aiden — great questions. Quick answers:
- Redaction: Yes — we support both client-side (SDK hook) redaction and server-side configurable redaction rules. For the PoC we can demo an SDK pre-send hook plus a server-side policy that strips PII fields (PII patterns configurable).
- KMS / CMKs: Supported. We can configure S3 exports to use your AWS CMK so Redwood never has access to your key material.
- Tagging & retention: Logs can be tagged at ingest (e.g., billing_event=true) so we can apply different retention policies per tag; we’ll include an example retention policy for 90/365 day buckets in the playbook.

Neha will follow up to lock in a technical deep-dive. In the meantime I’ve attached SOC2 summary and a short logging playbook (same as initial email). If Security has any specific evidence requests, please send them and we’ll pull the relevant artifacts.

Best,
Marissa
